content: 1. Both ozanimod and quinine are known to prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored in patients receiving these drugs concurrently. Due to the potential additive effects on heart rate, ozanimod treatment should generally not be initiated in patients already receiving QT-prolonging drugs with known arrhythmogenic properties. 2. The combination of ozanimod and quizartinib can increase the QTc interval. Therapy should be adjusted or monitored closely. Patients co-administered with QT-prolonging drugs should undergo more frequent ECG monitoring. 3. Both ozanimod and ranolazine increase the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Initiating ozanimod in patients concurrently treated with QT-prolonging drugs with arrhythmogenic properties is generally not recommended. 4. Co-administration of ozanimod and remestemcel-L may enhance immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Caution and monitoring are advised. When switching from drugs with prolonged immune effects, consider their half-life and mechanism of action to avoid unintended additive immunosuppressive effects. 5.
